items.title: Criminal IP Introduces AITEM as the Next Evolution of Attack Surface Management
items.author: Sponsored by Criminal IP
items.content: <article>Traditional attack surface management helps organizations discover exposed assets, but visibility alone is not enough to address threats. Criminal IP introduces AITEM, an AI-powered approach that connects exposure discovery with investigation, risk prioritization, and response. [...]</article>

items.title: Hackers abuse Google Ads, Bing redirects to push Claude ClickFix attacks
items.author: Lawrence Abrams
items.content: <article>Hackers are abusing legitimate Bing search-result redirects as click URLs in Google search ads to direct users to fake Claude installers that deliver ClickFix attacks. [...]</article>

items.title: Unpatched AhsayCBS flaws exploited to deploy webshells, mine crypto
items.author: Bill Toulas
items.content: <article>Threat actors are exploiting one critical and one medium-severity vulnerability still unpatched in the AhsayCBS backup management platform to deploy webshells and cryptocurrency miners. [...]</article>

items.title: FBI arrests another suspected ShinyHunters hacker after agency breach
items.author: Lawrence Abrams
items.content: <article>The FBI has arrested another suspected member of the ShinyHunters extortion group believed to be involved in the recent breach of FBI systems, Director Kash Patel announced Friday. [...]</article>

items.title: Germany arrests alleged core Qilin ransomware member after extradition
items.author: Bill Toulas
items.content: <article>Germany has arrested a Russian national suspected of being a leading member of the Qilin ransomware group following extradition from Japan earlier this month. [...]</article>

items.title: How to keep AI agents within their permissions
items.author: Sponsored by Token Security
items.content: <article>AI agents can use valid credentials to perform actions beyond their assigned permissions, creating risks that traditional access controls may not prevent. Token Security explains how organizations can enforce agent-specific policies without sacrificing autonomy. [...]</article>

items.title: Max severity SonicWall SMA1000 flaw now exploited in attacks
items.author: Sergiu Gatlan
items.content: <article>Attackers are exploiting a maximum-severity vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances (CVE-2026-102255) that was patched on Tuesday, three days ago. [...]</article>

items.title: Man admits to running network of 15,000 money mules for cybercriminals
items.author: Sergiu Gatlan
items.content: <article>​A Ukrainian-Russian dual citizen has pleaded guilty to running a massive money laundering operation that laundered millions for cybercriminals worldwide. [...]</article>

items.title: Microsoft: Outdated Windows devices will stop receiving security updates
items.author: Sergiu Gatlan
items.content: <article>Microsoft says devices running unsupported versions of Windows will stop receiving security updates after next year's Windows Update certificate rotation. [...]</article>

items.title: Citrix warns admins to patch new NetScaler RCE flaw immediately
items.author: Sergiu Gatlan
items.content: <article>Citrix has warned IT administrators to patch systems immediately against a new critical vulnerability affecting NetScaler ADC networking appliances and NetScaler Gateway secure remote access solutions. [...]</article>

items.title: Hackers get $1,262,000 for 98 zero-days at Pwn2Own Ireland
items.author: Sergiu Gatlan
items.content: <article>The Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 hacking contest has concluded, with hackers collecting $1,262,000 in rewards after exploiting 98 zero-day flaws. [...]</article>

items.title: FBI disrupts Chinese hacking tools used to breach critical infrastructure
items.author: Lawrence Abrams
items.content: <article>The FBI has seized seven domains used by Chinese state-sponsored hackers known as Flax Typhoon to operate two hacking tools, MicroScan and FishHub, used in attacks that breached critical infrastructure and other organizations worldwide. [...]</article>

items.title: Ransomware attack disrupts Japan's IDCF Cloud used by govt clients
items.author: Bill Toulas
items.content: <article>IDC Frontier, a major Japanese cloud and digital infrastructure company, disclosed that its IDCF Cloud service was targeted in a ransomware attack that caused an outage at a data center cluster serving the eastern part of the country. [...]</article>

items.title: Low-cost Android phones ship with residential proxy malware
items.author: Lawrence Abrams
items.content: <article>A malware campaign dubbed 'Midnight Mimosa' has been discovered on low-cost Android smartphones that ship with malicious software embedded in their firmware, allowing attackers to silently install apps, perform ad fraud, and turn devices into residential proxies. [...]</article>

items.title: FakeGit malware campaign returns with 17,610 malicious GitHub repos
items.author: Bill Toulas
items.content: <article>More than 17,000 fake repositories on GitHub are distributing the SmartLoader malware after the FakeGit campaign reactivated earlier this month to push the StealC infostealer. [...]</article>
